rule.borderline_note: Rows flagged borderline are the ones where the two readings genuinely compete. Every one carries the sentence that decided it, so a human can flip it and rerun.
rule.not_scheme: the money runs, builds, staffs or maintains an organisation or an asset, devolves general purpose funds to another tier of government, buys the capacity of the delivery system rather than the benefit, discharges the state's obligation to its own serving or retired staff, or is an accounting or adjustment head
rule.scheme: the money buys an identifiable benefit received by a person or household: cash, a kit, food, a scholarship, a fee waiver, a pension, insurance, a subsidy, a loan or its waiver, free travel, a house, treatment for a named beneficiary class, or training in which the trainee is himself the beneficiary
rule.two_lines_that_did_the_work: First, THE PRINTED DETAILED HEAD DECIDES when the row's own name does not. Odisha prints 8,562 sub-scheme names beneath the 1,628 codes and they are the nearest thing this corpus has to a purpose line: 'Welfare of Fishermen' is labelled not_scheme because the only detailed head printed under it is 'Development of Fisheries in collaboration with International Institutions', and 'Advertising, Sales and Publicity' is labelled a scheme because the only detailed head under it is 'Providing Free Mobile Phones to farmers'. Second, A MISSION IS NOT A SCHEME unless what it hands over is printed somewhere: Mission Vatsalya, Odisha Pusti Mission, Development of PVTGs and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan are all named for a beneficiary class, all carry a scheme marker, and all buy convergence, habitation works or service facilities. They are the errors that survive publication.

sampling: Stratified by DEPARTMENT FAMILY (WELFARE, SERVICE, ECONOMY, INFRA, GOVERNANCE, a fixed partition of the 44 demand books listed in parse/classify_odisha.py, taken from the lowest-numbered department on a row because 83 codes are funded in more than one) crossed with allocation band (nil, and quartiles of the 1,498 codes that carry an allocation), 25 non-empty strata. The 44 books cannot each be a stratum: 44 crossed with 5 bands is 220 cells and a sample large enough to fill them could not be labelled by hand. Within a stratum rows are sorted by scheme code and picked at even spacing, so the sample is reproducible without a random seed. Allocation is proportional to stratum size with a floor of 6, so the sample is close to self weighting; stratum_size and stratum_sampled are carried on every stratified row so a weighted estimate can be recomputed.

audit.what: Every row the classifier scores 4 or above that the stratified sample had not already covered. Together the two sets are a census of the published region and of the five bands below it, so the published list's precision is counted rather than estimated. The audit was made after the weights were fixed and was not fed back into them.

stratified.what: A probability sample of all 1,628 scheme codes. This is the only set the threshold sweep uses, because precision and recall estimated on anything else would not generalise to the rows the classifier has not seen.
